resources.string: First install: if accessibility is blocked by “Restricted settings”, allow it in MiDuo app info before enabling MiDuo Navigation gestures.

Only continue if you installed MiDuo from a trusted source. If Android reports “Restricted settings” or denies sensitive permissions: open MiDuo app info → More (⋮) → Allow restricted settings, then return to Accessibility → Downloaded apps → MiDuo Navigation gestures. On HyperOS, the installer may instead show “Allow the app to access permissions”; use its on-screen instructions. Names and availability vary by system version. MiDuo cannot approve this protection for you.

For navigation: activate MiDuo, set it as the default Home app and enable its accessibility service. MiDuo uses that service for Back, Home, Recents and opening system panels; it does not read screen content. Reading this guide is free; app-info and setup shortcuts require a MiDuo license.\n\nOptional: if the service stops in the background, review HyperOS autostart and battery restrictions. Approximate location is only needed for location-based features; selected wallpapers and widgets use their own system approval prompts. Do not enable every permission. MiDuo does not need contacts, SMS, microphone or unrestricted file access.

If HyperOS requires switching back to the system launcher, cancel and use MiDuo’s built-in Computer-free authorization. Enable Wireless debugging, enter the pairing code via the MiDuo Pair bubble, and enable gestures only after permission verification. No separate Shizuku app is needed. System security approval is still required; native Xiaomi animations are not guaranteed. This permission is separate from your MiDuo license.
Gesture mode enabled. Please test Back, Home and Recents; hiding the bar alone is not verification.
Set MiDuo as the default launcher first, then enable gestures.
